title: Prospective study on quality assurance in reconstructive allogeneic breast surgery after prophylactic mastectomy
summary: Patients with a genetic mutation (such as Angelina Jolie), which is associated with an increased risk of developing breast cancer, often opt to have the mammary gland removed in order to reduce the risk of cancer. During this operation, the gland is removed from under the skin and the breast is then rebuilt according to the woman's wishes. The woman's own tissue can be used for this, but breast implants are more common. This operation can sometimes lead to complications such as wound healing disorders and the death of areas of skin. This sometimes results in follow-up operations. The aim of our study is to evaluate risk factors for these complications.
conditions: Prophylactic surgery for risk-factors related to malignant neoplasms

interventions.name: A prospective cohort study is to be conducted at the Caritas Hospital St. Josef site. The study population consists of all patients for whom a prophylactic or therapeutic subcutaneous mastectomy is medically indicated. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Patients with indication for subcutaneous mastectomy (preservation of the skin mantle)
- Unilateral or bilateral removal of the mammary gland 
- With or without preservation of the nipple-areola complex (MAK)
- Unilateral or bilateral breast cancer 
- Purely prophylactic removal of the mammary gland 
- Direct allogeneic breast reconstruction
- Evidence of a genetic predisposition 
- Without evidence of a genetic mutation for tumor anxiety
Exclusion criteria:
- Two-stage procedure, e.g. with temporary insertion of an expander
- Reconstruction with autologous tissue 
- Patients <18 years of age 
- Patients in need of care / particularly vulnerable patients
